belongs_to: Printed answer to Figure it Out Q.5 (Section 1.3, book page 5): 'Can you think of pictorial ways to visualise the sequence of powers of 2? powers of 3?' - the powers-of-3 half ('Sequence of powers of 3 - One of the ways could be')
description: Dot-and-line pictures of the powers of 3, left to right, each labelled with its number printed below it (black font, plain dots = filled black circles). Printed in two rows because of width: first row holds 1, 3 and 9, second row holds 27. (1) Label '1': a single dot, no lines. (2) Label '3': a triangle with 3 dots at its corners (apex dot at top, two dots at the base corners), 3 edges, label below the middle. (3) Label '9': three triangles of the previous kind laid side by side in a row, 9 dots in all. Each triangle has a vertical left edge and two slanting edges meeting at an apex dot on its right (apex pointing right, like a play arrow). Counting: 3 top dots, 3 bottom dots, 3 apex dots = 9. Three long horizontal lines run through the whole figure: one through the 3 top dots, one through the 3 bottom dots, one through the 3 apex dots (the first triangle's top and bottom dots are joined to the next triangle's by these lines; the third triangle ends the figure). Label '9' sits under the middle triangle. (4) Label '27' (second row, label centred below the figure): a wide, flat, perspective drawing of 27 dots = 3 blocks side by side, each block being 9 dots = the same 'three right-pointing triangles' as in the 9 picture but drawn in 3D perspective, so the 3 triangles of a block step diagonally down and to the right (top-left, then lower and right of it, then lower again), corresponding corners of consecutive triangles in a block joined by thick lines, so each block looks like a slanted triangular prism. Per block: triangle 1 dots (top-left, bottom-left, apex), triangle 2 and triangle 3 likewise, 3 triangles x 3 dots = 9 dots. The 3 blocks (27 dots total, counted 9+9+9) are placed one after the other horizontally and are joined to each other by thin grey straight horizontal lines running from every one of a block's 9 dots to the matching dot of the next block (the top-left dot of block 1, block 2 and block 3 lie on one horizontal line, and so on). Block 3 is the right-most; the lines end there. No axes, no colours (black on white).
unclear: The exact number of thin grey connecting lines in the 27 drawing was not counted line by line; one per dot of a block (9) is the expectation from the 27 = 3 x 9 structure.
The book prints 1, 3, 9 on one row and 27 on the next row; the 27 drawing is the same sequence, not a separate figure.

belongs_to: Printed answer to Figure it Out Q.5 (Section 1.3, book page 5): powers-of-2 half, introduced as 'Sequence of powers of 2 - given on page 6' (the answer prints the picture as well)
description: Dot-and-line pictures of the powers of 2, left to right, each with its number printed below (1, 2, 4, 8, 16 on one row; 32 on a row below). Black dots on black lines on white. (1) Label '1': one dot. (2) Label '2': two dots joined by one short horizontal line (2 dots, 1 edge). (3) Label '4': a square with a dot at each corner (4 dots, 4 edges). (4) Label '8': a cube drawn in oblique projection as two equal squares offset diagonally (one upper-left, one lower-right) with the 4 pairs of matching corners joined by short slanting edges; 8 dots, 12 edges. (5) Label '16': two such cubes, the first at upper-left and the second further down and to the right along a diagonal, 8 dots each, 16 dots in all; the 8 dots of cube 1 are joined to the 8 matching dots of cube 2 by 8 long thin grey parallel slanting lines (down-right), so the figure looks like a long box of 2 cubes. (6) Label '32' (separate row, label under the second cube): four cubes in a diagonal line from top-left to bottom-right, 8 dots each, 4 x 8 = 32 dots in all, the matching corners of all four cubes joined by 8 long thin grey parallel slanting lines running from the first to the fourth cube through the corresponding corners of the cubes between. Cubes are the same size in 8, 16 and 32. No axes, no colours.
unclear: The thin grey connecting lines in 16 and 32 were taken as 8 (one per cube corner); not each line was individually counted.
The label '2' is printed a little to the right of its line segment and '4' is printed in a lighter font; these are layout details only.

belongs_to: Printed answer to Figure it out Q.1 (Section 1.4, book page 7): 'Can you find a similar pictorial explanation for why adding counting numbers up and down, i.e. 1, 1 + 2 + 1, 1 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 1, ..., gives square numbers?' - 'Ans. One of the ways is-'
description: A row of four dot-lattice diamonds (squares turned 45 degrees, dots = filled black circles joined by straight diagonal lines), growing left to right, bottom edges roughly aligned. (1) Label '1' under it: a single dot. (2) Label '1+2+1' with '= 4' on the line below: a tilted square with 4 dots (1 dot at top, 2 dots in the middle row left and right, 1 dot at the bottom), 4 edges, 1 small diamond cell. Rows of dots from top: 1, 2, 1. (3) Label '1+2+3+2+1' with '= 9' on the line below: a larger tilted square lattice of 9 dots, rows of dots from top 1, 2, 3, 2, 1; the middle dot is joined to 4 neighbours; 4 small diamond cells (2 x 2). (4) NO label: the largest tilted lattice of 16 dots, rows of dots from top 1, 2, 3, 4, 3, 2, 1 (counted 1+2+3+4+3+2+1 = 16), a 4 x 4 dot array turned 45 degrees with 9 small diamond cells (3 x 3); each interior dot is joined to its 4 diagonal neighbours, edge dots to 2. Below the row, outside the picture, the answer line prints the sequence '1, 1 + 2 + 1, 1 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 1, ...,'. The dots in each diamond are the square numbers 1, 4, 9, 16: the diagonal rows of dots are the counting numbers going up then down. No axes, no colours (black on white).
unclear: The fourth (16-dot) diamond has no printed label or sum; its row counts were verified by counting (1,2,3,4,3,2,1 = 16).
